= Ordered Metadata transport

Client::start_ordered_metadata submits named-topic Metadata requests on the producer's existing authenticated librdkafka connection.
The producer must have a NativeByteAccount installed before creation.
The operation uses the first selected Up broker's negotiated Metadata API range, capped at version 13.
A disabled auto-creation setting requires version 4 or later.
An absent ready broker returns BrokerNotReady without accepting work; the native sparse-connection machinery schedules connection attempts.
The caller bounds readiness retries separately from the accepted request's deadline.
The named-topic entry point requires at least one topic.
Client::start_ordered_metadata_brokers sends an explicit empty topic array with the same completion and admission contracts.
It requires version 1 or later because version 0 interprets that array as a request for every topic.
The legacy array count is zero and its compact equivalent is one, distinct from the compact null marker.
The broker's existing flexible request finalizer appends the empty body tag count after the authorization flags.
Both entry points reject unsupported profiles and invalid lengths.
Ordinary fetch_metadata, MetadataRequest wrappers, native cache parsing and their version ceilings are unchanged.

`Client::start_ordered_metadata_at` submits the named or broker-only form to one learned native broker selected by its nonnegative node ID.
The inventory lookup retains that broker while the client lock is held and returns `BrokerNotReady` for an absent, non-Up or terminating target.
Sparse connection scheduling can start the existing target's initial connection.
The request uses the selected native broker owner through completion and retries.
The same owner can change its advertised endpoint and reconnect.

`Client::start_ordered_metadata_endpoint` submits the same forms to an authenticated configured bootstrap broker matched by its exact native host bytes and unsigned port.
Set `enable.ordered.metadata.bootstrap=true` when constructing the producer to keep configured broker owners available throughout its lifetime.
Discovery can retain both a configured owner and a learned owner for the same address.
The producer's normal connection scheduling and byte account govern both owners.
Endpoint submissions require this mode.
The caller supplies the bytes as configured in the broker inventory, including any retained IPv6 brackets.
The broker lock captures the negotiated Metadata version and socket generation while the current configured endpoint matches the connected address epoch.
The broker thread checks the socket generation before queueing and again before transmitting.
Missing endpoints return BrokerNotReady and an accepted request reports a stale connection as a terminal transport error.
The caller owns connection establishment, Java bootstrap identity mapping and rescheduling after failure.

== Ownership and release

OrderedMetadataRequest is a passive owner of a C completion reference and an Arc of the producer's actual native byte account.
The C completion is a passive handoff with a mutex protecting reference count and one terminal publication.
It owns one allocation containing its record and a fixed body-capacity region.
The account acquires that allocation's complete size before calloc.
An encoded request scratch buffer acquires a separate exact charge before malloc and releases it after the accounted sender has copied the request.
The sender's request buffer and every XMIT_BUF, XMIT_RETRY and RECV_BUF node retain the existing independent final-free charges.
Client-ID/header and complete request size validation run before completion admission.

The accepted operation and Rust caller hold separate completion references.
Retries retain the operation reference through the absolute deadline, including a nested inline retry-node denial.
On the any-broker and learned-ID routes a transport, timeout or broker request-timeout error retries through the native retry path when permitted by that deadline and the existing request retry limit.
An endpoint request has one socket generation and completes without a native retry.
Terminal publication records the original native error before considering body-copy errors.
A successful body must fit the pre-admitted completion capacity and be fully readable; excess size reports MSG_SIZE_TOO_LARGE and a missing or truncated body reports BAD_MSG.
The callback allocates no output and invokes no Rust closure, destructor or waker.
The last native completion reference destroys the mutex and allocation before returning its account charge.

The Rust destructor releases its C reference before its account Arc.
Dropping an async wait leaves the request pollable; dropping the request abandons delivery while the native operation remains bounded by its deadline or producer teardown.
A completed raw response remains readable after producer destruction because its request handle retains the account.
Native request, response and queue owners may remain live after terminal publication or after the caller drops the result.
Their charges remain until their own final frees, independently of the completion record.
NativeByteAccount remains a Monitor Object whose clients == 0 && used == 0 condition controls last-guard release on the Rust caller.
The existing blocking last-account-drop contract still applies.

== Borrowed response access

rd_kafka_req_response initializes its reader after the eight-byte response size/correlation header, copies the request's flexible flag, and consumes flexible response-header tags before invoking the custom completion.
Ordered request callback identity selects a borrowed header reader matching ResponseHeaderData and ByteUtils; ordinary requests retain their existing header path.
The ordered header reader consumes at most five bytes per varint, truncates the fifth terminal byte into Java int bits, and checks nonnegative counts/sizes and the 10,000-tag limit.
Unknown tag IDs may repeat, decrease or decode to negative Java ints.
A native header parse failure reaches the existing error callback path as BAD_MSG before body publication.
The custom completion copies the remaining body before rd_kafka_parse_Metadata or the metadata cache can sort any partition array.

MetadataView validates every known field and nested tag before exposing a visitor.
It covers versions 0 through 13 with the generated MetadataResponseData reader's signed length arithmetic and failure order.
Strings are limited to 32767 bytes; any negative nullable string length represents null.
Compact length subtraction wraps as a Java int, including a fifth terminal varint byte whose high bits are discarded.
Array and tag counts must be nonnegative and no greater than the remaining byte count before their respective 1,000,000-element and 10,000-tag ceilings are checked.
Tag payload sizes must be nonnegative and fit the remaining source.
An unconsumed suffix is accepted by the Java response wrapper and retained by raw(); trailing_bytes() exposes it separately.
The visitor's second pass borrows broker, cluster, topic, UUID, partition, replica, ISR, offline-replica, authorization, throttle and raw error fields in wire order.
Duplicate entries and signed error/ID/epoch values remain unmodified.
Leader epochs are present from v7, while has_reliable_leader_epochs follows Java's v9 threshold.
Unknown flexible body tags, including duplicate, decreasing and negative IDs, remain in received order in raw bytes.
The MetadataView facade returns UnsupportedUtf8 for malformed strings, at the original field-read position before later fields can fail.
RawMetadataView preserves those strings as borrowed byte slices through RawBroker, RawTopic and RawEvent.
OrderedMetadataRequest::poll_raw and wait_raw expose this view from the same native completion and retain its existing account lifetime.
Both views use one checked cursor with a compile-time UTF8-validation profile.
Raw string lengths and Summary.string_bytes describe the original wire payload, before replacement expansion.
The raw view accepts malformed UTF8 without normalizing or re-encoding the body; Java replacement decoding and output admission belong to the producer metadata owner.
The cursor, event views, array iterator and summary are passive call-local borrowed values with no output heap owner.
Caller-side collections require their own admission before construction.

== Allocation domain

The completion record, fixed copied-body capacity and temporary request encoding join the account's existing request/frame/queue domain.
At every instant their combined native allocation charges share the fixed pre-admitted account ceiling.
Receive frames still acquire admission before correlation, including late and partial responses.
Copying a response retains both the source frame and completion capacity until their separate owners release them.
Validation does not allocate an output collection or grow a buffer.
The caller owns the topic-input array, any application result, and runtime timer/task allocation used by wait.

The attached account also tracks ApiVersions handshake request buffers and the broker's decoded and fallback array payloads through their respective final release.
The ordinary Metadata parser admits its root arena and any additional storage segments before allocation and keeps their charges with the result after transfer.
Retained native topic-cache arenas also acquire the actual client account before allocation and release it at their common final free.
Ordinary Metadata rack computation also admits its temporary matching-rack pointer buffer on that same account.
Native client construction, bootstrap and discovered broker growth, broker threads and stacks, independent clones and their rack scratch, admin output copies, native sort internals, TLS/SASL, ordinary outbound requests, allocator overhead and the monitor require separate bounds.
A whole-producer bound still requires a separately pre-admitted construction/background domain or admission interception for every reachable owner in that domain.
Neither the completion cap nor borrowed validation establishes that bound.
Java snapshot retention and partial/full merge, UUID/leader-epoch state, HashMap encounter order, metadata refresh/throttle scheduling, per-topic signed RoundRobin counters and once-per-send explicit partition binding remain separate integration work.
The Java RoundRobinPartitioner class is not activated by this transport.

The raw-string integration fixture configures malformed rack bytes through the existing native mock API, observes the original bytes through poll_raw, retains the UTF8 facade's error and keeps the raw result through producer destruction.
The broker-only sources check the v0 exclusion, v1 and v4 negotiation floors and explicit empty wire counts.
The native mock integration fixture creates an existing topic and verifies that broker-only Metadata returns the broker and zero topics, including when read after producer destruction.
The targeted lookup cases distinguish two broker owners, unavailable or terminating targets and balanced references.
The targeted mock integration submits named and broker-only requests to learned IDs and checks missing-target readiness with other brokers already usable.
The endpoint source fixtures distinguish configured and learned brokers at the same address, check exact host and port, reject a changed address epoch and pass a stale socket generation through the actual broker send loop.
The endpoint mock source fixture uses the configured bootstrap address and keeps the result through producer destruction.
Additional raw-view sources retain all supported versions, nullable names, original string-size ceilings, tag/suffix bytes, and validation before visitation.
All previously published assertions remain unchanged.
Compilation, formatting, project scripts and runtime tests were not executed under the Phase 1 work order.


== Native connection observations

Client::observe_native_connection samples an existing learned broker ID through that broker's actual op queue.
Client::observe_native_endpoint samples an exact configured endpoint and requires hidden enable.ordered.metadata.bootstrap=true so ordinary discovery retains that configured owner.
Neither call connects, resolves an address or chooses another broker.
The C native record and each queued control are admitted independently on the producer's actual byte account before allocation and handoff.
A disabled queue can complete cancellation inline while the caller still owns its record reference.
Queued abandonment and teardown release the control, temporary target reference and record at their own final ownership boundaries.
Accounted control allocation is fallible and rolls back its charge; legacy unaccounted op allocation retains its assert-on-failure policy.

Only the pending control holds a broker reference.
A ready record stores immutable copied native facts and does not retain that broker, so keeping it cannot prevent real decommission.
The result's Rust owner borrows NativeClient and retains its account Arc; it must be dropped before that client.
The caller owns polling/readiness deadlines and drops nonselected observations at the end of its attempt.
A completed native request returned by into_metadata has the existing independent request/account lifetime.

A new native owner serial is assigned before configured/learned broker publication under the existing client write lock.
Configured creation is serialized by brokers_add0 and learned creation by broker_update.
Internal and logical brokers do not consume the counter.
Failed broker creation consumes its serial, and a saturated counter gives later owners zero without wraparound or changing ordinary native creation behavior.
That serial is native provenance scoped to one live client, not a Java identity hash or an allocation address.
The separate socket generation remains the connection witness; zero and saturated socket generations cannot qualify submission.

NativeConnectionObservation::into_metadata consumes the observation and locates only its copied owner serial in the originating client's inventory.
It verifies the observed native UP state/transport, current native UP state, same node/source, unchanged address/connect epochs and exact socket generation before constructing a request.
A replacement owner with the same node ID and a restarted socket generation does not qualify.
The accepted request reuses the actor enqueue and actual send-loop generation fence and never reconnects or retries after transport failure or timeout.
The ID-only and configured-endpoint entry points retain their existing separate contracts.

The copied snapshot exposes native source/state codes, socket/owner serials, native monotonic microseconds, transport presence, queue counts, maximum native in-flight window and whether the outgoing head was partially sent.
State codes are the pinned librdkafka broker enum: INIT0, DOWN1, TRY_CONNECT2, CONNECT3, SSL_HANDSHAKE4, AUTH_LEGACY5, UP6, APIVERSION_QUERY7, AUTH_HANDSHAKE8, AUTH_REQ9 and REAUTH10.
A native UP snapshot with no transport does not establish channel readiness.
Native timestamps are not Java epoch milliseconds, and native queue counts are not NetworkClient's in-flight request deque.
No native throttle average supplies Java's throttle deadline.
Snapshots from different broker actors are not one serialized NetworkClient scan.

The pinned NetworkClient/ClusterConnectionStates/InFlightRequests/Selector sources require Java random, throttle, channel, send-completion and reconnect chronology observations that these native facts alone do not establish.
This transport does not implement ConnectionObservations or replace any missing Java observation with a guessed false, zero, native jitter or native count.
The producer updater owns their qualification and remains a separate activation boundary.
Client/broker construction and background memory, other controls, DNS/TLS/SASL machinery, native cache scratch and independent clones, and allocator overhead still require their own admission proof.
The fixed observation/control charges do not close whole-native, source-completeness or Phase2 gates.

Additive native sources cover serial exhaustion, half-allocation cleanup, cancellation/publication, exact-owner/epoch/socket fences and a real broker decommission while its ready observation remains retained.
The MockCluster source fixture establishes a learned native connection, uses the safe observation and consuming submission APIs, and retains the completed request after producer destruction.
The fixtures have not been compiled or executed in the source-only phase.

== Ordinary Metadata cache retained values

A full ordinary native cache entry owns every rack array/string that it retains, including force_racks data when this client has no rack and nonnull zero-length array presence.
The reliable-epoch merge owns each selected replica/ISR array and retains its existing optional-rack behavior.
A replacement preserves the source epoch choice, maximum physical partition extent, incoming logical count and aligned arena seed.
Cached values survive the parsed Metadata arena's destruction and the replaced entry's final free.
Public parsed Metadata ownership and ordered native observation APIs retain their separate contracts.

Additive regression sources cover full/merged pointee lifetime, absent versus present empty arrays, old/new/new-only epoch winners, and source physical/logical partition counts.
The actual native main actor also runs ordinary and admin parser fixtures and checks retained cache values after releasing their independent parsed arenas.
Rack-aware topic-info copies initialize a zero rack count for every partition with an absent rack list before comparing assignments.
Those fixtures use existing native actor queues and client teardown rather than fabricated actor identities or abandoned thread handles.
The source fixtures have not been compiled or executed.

Each cache entry is one passive client-owned arena with its own account pointer and exact allocation charge.
Full and reliable-merge sizing checks multiplication, eight-byte rounding and total addition before admission or allocation.
The charge covers the entry, copied topic name, physical public/internal partition arrays and every retained rack, replica and ISR extent with its individual padding.
The reliable merge retains its original extra root seed and maximum physical extent even when the new logical partition count is smaller.
Zero-count pointer presence retains its source geometry without adding a payload extent.
An accounted allocation uses fallible malloc and releases admission on failure.
The builder borrows the allocator for one call.

A replacement admits all new storage while the old arena is still live and charged.
Admission or allocation denial returns the typed DENIED outcome before changing the old name/UUID indexes, expiry links, timestamps or payload.
Successful construction assigns the new arena to the actual client account rather than copying a lease from its source entry.
Replacement, explicit deletion, expiry, hint purge and client teardown all free the arena before releasing its charge through the common destructor.
Cache purge and final destruction precede the client's account detach.
The account guard's final drain covers these retained arenas.

The shared ordinary/admin parser admits additional decoded storage when the initial arena fills.
Array counts must fit the response before they can request decoded storage.
The parsed metadata owner keeps its admitted segments alive through final destruction.
An admission denial returns CRIT_SYS_RESOURCE and no parsed Metadata owner.
Broker inventory changes and earlier topic/cache updates have already happened.
The denied topic's live-topic update precedes its failed cache construction, so that topic may have new live state beside its previous valid cache entry.
Live topics copy timestamps, errors, states, UUIDs and leader/epoch integers, allocate their own partition owners and retain broker references explicitly.
The error path purges requested hints, wakes observers and schedules expiry for any earlier accepted cache writes, then releases the parsed arena.
It skips later successful-response freshness, controller, cluster and group stages.
The ordinary response handler reports the original permanent resource error to its requesting op, and both admin parsers return it before output projection.
Independent admin/assignor copies and live-topic growth still need their own admission.
Topic-info projection has the separate account and activation contract below.

Hint storage is optional suppression state.
A denied eligible topic still enters a nonnull query destination, and the returned hint count includes only installed arenas.
Denied upgrades preserve the existing NOENT or WAIT_CACHE value and expiry facts.
Callers without a query destination rely on their retained topic or subscription interest for a later attempt.
Accepted hints in a mixed batch remain installed when a later hint is denied.

Seven additive direct source fixtures cover checked layout, exact and one-byte-short bounds, fallible allocation rollback, account provenance, old/new overlap, zero-length geometry, mixed hint denial and final disposal routes.
Two ordinary-handler cases and four actual admin-parser cases exercise denial on the first or second topic after the response arena has been admitted.
They check the original error, empty output, requested-hint cleanup, earlier cache retention, observer delivery, expiry scheduling, skipped freshness and final account balance.
The deterministic fixtures own their caller-thread identity, native locks, timers, queues and account directly.
A Rust source dispatcher registers this native slice.
Cache scratch, independent clones and other native owners require separate admission.

The lightweight topic conversion acquires the client write lock before looking up or creating a proper topic.
The constructor holds it through local topic publication, cache lookup and initialization from the cached entry.
A source fixture observes that lock through the immediate constructor diagnostic on the native main actor and checks that the new topic inherits cached metadata after the parsed response has been freed.
Native request and cache scratch, assignor and admin clones, allocator overhead and runtime effects require separate qualification.

The Fetch and Produce leader tag handler holds the client write lock from cache lookup through leader and local topic updates.
When a tag changes cached leader metadata, the handler reacquires the client write lock after processing the topics to notify cache observers and schedule expiry.
A source fixture on the actual native main actor checks the lock on a missing-broker diagnostic, the accepted UUID update and observer wakeup, and the stale name-addressed update.

When the consumer-group Metadata refresh finds no usable broker, it holds the client write lock while replacing request-in-progress hints with retry hints for the next refresh.
A native main-actor fixture checks the lock at both hint insertion diagnostics.
It verifies that the retry hint's recorded expiry is one socket timeout after insertion and that the expiry timer stays unarmed.

== Independent topic-info projections

Metadata's literal and wildcard projection loops copy each selected topic into an independent topic-info arena while their client read lock protects the source cache.
The accounted constructor measures its root, copied topic name, present rack arrays and strings, and the internal partition array required when any rack list is present.
Checked products, individual eight-byte rounding and aggregate sums precede account acquisition and fallible allocation.
For a non-NULL account, the copied owner retains the actual client's complete arena charge through candidate-list comparison, effective-list retention and common final destruction.
It frees the arena before returning its charge.
Equal candidates are destroyed after comparison, and changed candidates are admitted while the previous effective list is still live.
Source cache replacement or purge cannot invalidate the copied name or rack values.

Both Metadata projection functions return a typed native error, with CRIT_SYS_RESOURCE on a denied topic-info arena.
The caller owns any partial info and error lists produced before that failure.
Both classic consumer-group callers discard those transient lists and publish the existing asynchronous consumer resource error before effective-topic comparison, topic-error normalization, revocation or join.
They retain the last complete effective/error lists and assignments.
The cooperative subscription path has already installed its new subscription intent and incremented the version before projection.
Its successful return transfers that adopted input away from the requesting SUBSCRIBE op, even when effective projection failed asynchronously.
The new intent remains beside the previous effective list until a later complete projection replaces it.
The shared Metadata parser retains its existing void consumer-group notification contract, so native Metadata can finish successfully while this later effective projection reports its separate asynchronous failure.

The retained list is owned by the serialized consumer-group actor and is cleared or replaced before final group destruction.
The built-in range, roundrobin and sticky member-metadata callbacks synchronously copy topic names into their own encoded storage.
Those encoded outputs, candidate-list and topic-error scratch, consumer error ops/strings, full Metadata copies and their rack scratch, and other assignor/admin owners still require separate admission.

The default set_native_byte_account profile supports producers only.
The explicit set_native_byte_account_with_consumers profile also constructs native consumers with the actual shared account, so classic consumer-group projection callers can use this admission path.
NULL-account callers retain their legacy behavior.
The deterministic consumer fixtures exercise the internal fallible copy boundary with an internal account and caller-thread group state.
Application call-site activation retains its own capacity and configuration policy.
They cover exact and short admission, malloc rollback, rack geometry and lifetime, old/new overlap, partial projection prefixes, complete projections, both consumer failure paths, adopted input ownership, equal/changed effective lists, built-in member-metadata lifetime and final group destruction.

== Ordinary Metadata rack computation

For each partition with replicas, the ordinary Metadata helper counts the nonnull rack pointers found in the parsed broker array before allocating scratch storage.
A passive call-local owner holds one exact pointer buffer and its account charge; its native list header stays on the stack.
Checked pointer products and the native list-count limit precede account acquisition and allocation.
A denied account or failed malloc returns the existing native resource error.
NULL-account clients retain the native aborting allocation policy.
Zero matches allocate no scratch, while retaining the existing present-empty output array for a nonempty replica list and the absent output for a zero-replica list.

The buffer borrows rack strings from the unpublished parsed root and segments.
The same native list sort and string comparator determine lexical order and the representative pointer for equal rack values.
Compaction retains the full allocated capacity until the buffer is freed.
The unique output array uses the existing parsed Metadata allocator while scratch is still charged, so a new output segment requires admission for both allocations at once.
The helper frees scratch before releasing its charge on every success and failure return.
The root and segments continue to own all retained rack text and output arrays through final Metadata destruction.
The sorting library's internal storage has a separate admission obligation.

The shared ordinary/admin parser reaches rack computation after decoding the response and updating broker inventory.
A denial preserves those broker changes and all earlier topic/cache updates, and occurs before the current topic's live-topic or cache update.
It returns CRIT_SYS_RESOURCE with NULL parsed output, purges requested hints, propagates earlier cache changes, schedules their expiry and destroys the parsed root and segments.
It retains the existing output-count-before-output-pointer order if output allocation fails after scratch succeeds.
No rollback of the earlier mutation prefix is promised.

The unexecuted source fixtures compare the native sort/dedup value and representative-pointer geometry, test checked sizing, zero and duplicate racks, exact/short admission, malloc rollback, bounded appends and scratch/output-segment overlap.
Eight ordinary/admin parser profiles cover first/later denial with and without a requested hint, retained previous cache values, observer delivery, expiry, unchanged freshness and final account balance.
They use one indexed fixture broker with the response's exact existing ID and endpoint, so broker update needs neither a replacement thread nor a queued node update.
This slice does not activate accounted consumer construction, charge independent full Metadata clone scratch or establish a whole-native bound.
